name: Moon
description: Earth's natural satellite. Surface craters are often easiest to see near the boundary between light and shadow.

name: Mercury
description: The innermost planet. Observing near the Sun requires specialist planning; this prototype does not control a telescope.

name: Venus
description: A rocky planet with a dense atmosphere. Through a telescope its illuminated phase changes.

name: Mars
description: A rocky planet whose iron-rich surface gives it a reddish appearance.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet in our Solar System. Bright planetary images may need a nearby star field for plate solving.

name: Saturn
description: A gas giant surrounded by rings. The rings are mostly particles of ice.

name: Uranus
description: An ice giant. Small telescope images may show an unresolved dot; appearance alone cannot confirm its identity.

name: Neptune
description: The outermost of the eight planets. Its small apparent size makes verified position important for identification.

name: Sirius
description: The brightest star in the night sky, in Canis Major.

name: Canopus
description: A luminous southern star in Carina.

name: Arcturus
description: An orange giant in Bootes. Its color reflects a cooler surface than the Sun.

name: Vega
description: A bright star in Lyra and one corner of the Summer Triangle.

name: Capella
description: A multiple-star system in Auriga.

name: Rigel
description: A blue supergiant in Orion; brightness estimates vary.

name: Procyon
description: A nearby binary system in Canis Minor.

name: Betelgeuse
description: A variable red supergiant in Orion. Its listed magnitude is illustrative, not a current measurement.

name: Altair
description: A rapidly rotating star in Aquila and a corner of the Summer Triangle.

name: Aldebaran
description: An orange giant in Taurus, seen in the direction of the Hyades cluster.

name: Spica
description: A bright binary star in Virgo.

name: Antares
description: A variable red supergiant in Scorpius.

name: Pollux
description: An orange giant in Gemini.

name: Fomalhaut
description: A bright star in Piscis Austrinus with a surrounding debris disk.

name: Deneb
description: A luminous supergiant in Cygnus and a corner of the Summer Triangle.

name: Regulus
description: A bright multiple-star system in Leo.

name: Polaris
description: A variable star close to the north celestial pole. It is not exactly at the pole.
